subject: Proposal: Flexible Prepay Transition & Ramp Guardrails for Valence Bio
messages:
From: Anna Delgado <anna@valencebio.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Valence Bio Procurement <procurement@valencebio.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Switching billing cadence — looking at annual prepay options

Hi Sergio,

We run a fairly bursty R&D workload that peaks Q1/Q4; currently on monthly usage billing. The finance team is open to an annual prepay if we can get predictable unit economics and protection for ramp variability.

Can you share what a transition would look like from monthly to an annual prepay for ~$180k ARR current run-rate, and the kinds of term discounts (multi-year?) and ramp credits you offer for a first-year ramp? Also need to know what happens if our usage spikes above the committed baseline in month 2 or month 9.

Attached is our last 12 months usage export for context.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Delgado
Procurement Lead, Valence Bio
attachment: Valence_Annual_Usage_Report.csv (csv)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anna Delgado <anna@valencebio.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Switching billing cadence — looking at annual prepay options

Hi Anna — thanks for the usage file, that helps a lot. High-level proposal below; attaching a one-pager and a sample term sheet.

Summary proposal (initial):
- Term: 12-month prepay, option to extend to 24-month for deeper discount.
- Commitment: start at 1.0x current run-rate (~$180k) with staged ramp protection (see below).
- Pricing tiers: 10% standard term discount for 12-month prepay; 16% if you commit to 24 months.
- Ramp protection: For months 1–3 we’ll apply a 25% overage buffer at the committed rate (i.e., you only pay committed rate for usage up to 125% of baseline). Months 4–6 buffer drops to 112.5%, then normalizes. This keeps early-stage spikes predictable.
- True-ups: Quarterly true-up with crediting for any sustained under-utilization.
- Additional concession: First-year adoption credit of $15k to offset initial lock-in risk (applied as monthly bill credit or one-time invoice credit).

Notes and ask:
- If you need hard SLA credits for latency-sensitive endpoints or SOC/integration work, that can be scoped separately.
- Can you confirm whether procurement needs DocuSign or a PO process before we execute?

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-Valence-2026.pdf (proposal), sample_term_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Anna Delgado <anna@valencebio.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Switching billing cadence — looking at annual prepay options

Sergio — this looks promising. A few clarifying Qs from finance & engineering:

1) What happens to the overage price beyond the 125% buffer in months 1–3? Is it billed at the committed per-unit rate or at list?
2) If we move to a 24-month term and hit a sustained 150% usage in months 9–12 due to a product launch, will you credit any portion retroactively or do we just pay the overage?
3) Can the $15k adoption credit be split into months (we prefer smoothing credits against monthly invoices)?

Procurement typically needs a PO and a signed DocuSign PDF. I cc'd procurement@valencebio.com earlier; they will open a PO once terms are agreed.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call this week if that helps.

—Anna
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Switching billing cadence — looking at annual prepay options

Laura / Markus — forwarding Valence's follow-up. Key asks:
- Need an answer on overage pricing beyond buffer (months 1–3): engineering wants committed per-unit or list?
- Confirm whether we can offer retroactive credit for sustained >140% usage in months 9–12 on a 24-month commit (they're worried about product launch risk).
- Approve splitting the $15k adoption credit over 12 monthly invoice credits.

My recommendation:
- Overage billed at committed per-unit up to 150% for year 1; beyond that list price applies. This makes early spikes cheap but protects us.
- For 24-month term: offer a one-time launch protection credit up to 10% of additional overage if triggered (requires pre-notification of launch window).
- Split $15k as $1,250 credit/mo for the first 12 months.

If you approve I'll send an updated term sheet and get Laura in to finalize DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Sergio
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Please send updated term sheet to Valence and loop procurement. I'll review final DocuSign before sending.
